9.speaker: Player
9.text: “You still have to prove that you make returns on your deals. Our investment in Armadine had better make a return.”

10.speaker: Gus Manger
10.text: “I never claim to see the future, President Rayne. I merely find good opportunities and seize them.”

11.speaker: Player
11.text: “The discussions were lively during the highway contract award. I'm willing to hear new offers from you.”

12.speaker: Gus Manger
12.text: “And I'm willing to present them. Despite your unfortunate choice of the H-3 over the L-1.”

27.speaker: Gus Manger
27.text: "Please come this way. Ewald and I have some exciting news to share with you."

28.speaker: Gus Manger
28.text: “The corruption in that organization is unfathomable. Makes the Lotherberg group look like saints.”

29.speaker: Gus Manger
29.text: “By the way, I still don't believe Taurus should be trusted with such a monumental mega-project.”

30.speaker: Gus Manger
30.text: “I'm glad you contracted Underhall, by the way. You won't be disappointed.”

31.speaker: Player
31.text: “The government has clear control over SSC's operations. We wouldn't get that with a private corporation.”

32.speaker: Player
32.text: “I have to take the safe option this early in the term, Mr. Manger.”

33.speaker: Player
33.text: “I think it's time we let fresh -- and fast -- new faces have a shot.”

34.speaker: Player
34.text: “Status quos are meant to be broken. I want to be the change maker during my term.”

35.speaker: Player
35.text: “It seemed the least risky option. We need safe bets.”

36.speaker: Player
36.text: “The workers need to be protected somehow. We can't ignore that problem.”

37.speaker: Gus Manger
37.text: “It might seem like we have control, but those organizations are slow and inflexible.”

38.speaker: Gus Manger
38.text: “I admit I'm slightly frustrated that you contracted SSC. They've been leeching off the Sordish people for too long.”

39.speaker: Gus Manger
39.text: “They need to walk before they can run. And I'm saying this as a guy who actually almost likes Frens Ricter."

40.speaker: Gus Manger
40.text: “Calculated risks, Mr. President. Taurus is not the right call. But don't mind me."

41.speaker: Gus Manger
41.text: “It's a pity you only had three choices, to be honest.”

42.speaker: Player
42.text: “The SSC is one of our national treasures. It rebuilt most of Sordland in the '30s.”

43.speaker: Gus Manger
43.text: “Understandable. But we have to break the cycle at some point if we want to stick around.”

44.speaker: Gus Manger
44.text: “Yes, nobody can deny the SSC's great work for our people in the Restoration period. But those days are long gone.”

45.speaker: Narrator
45.text: He pushed open a door. We walked down yet another hallway, seemingly in the direction we'd just come from.

46.speaker: Gus Manger
46.text: “Like a maze, isn't it? That's Qinali architecture for you."

47.speaker: Gus Manger
47.text: “The only difference between an SSC manager and a fossil from the pre-Migration period is that the fossil might actually be worth something.”

48.speaker: Narrator
48.text: A stark contrast to the blue-collar workers outside working with machinery, transportation, and maintenance.

50.speaker: Gus Manger
50.text: “To be 100 percent honest, Mr. President, I doubted he even wanted to discuss this with you.”

51.speaker: Gus Manger
51.text: “We do have to be delicate with Gasom, though. A corporation this big is like a house of cards."

53.speaker: Player
53.text: “Does the average working-class man in Narbel really give a damn about that?”

54.speaker: Player
54.text: “We won't know until they complete the project. There's no reason to be negative before then.”

55.speaker: Gus Manger
55.text: “I respect that. Most of my life has been about changing the status quo in Gruni.”

56.speaker: Gus Manger
56.text: “Time will tell. I also hope that it will succeed, believe me.”

57.speaker: Player
57.text: “I still have my doubts, but I'll take your word for now.”

58.speaker: Gus Manger
58.text: “I'm just a civil servant who wants what's best for the Sordish people.”

59.speaker: Gus Manger
59.text: “But there's a time and a place to take risks. The stock market, yes. National infrastructure, no.”

63.speaker: Gus Manger
63.text: “Admittedly, I'm biased. But I do think Gasom is extraordinary.”

64.speaker: Player
64.text: “We worked closely in the past and are on friendly terms. I'm open to see what we can do.”

65.speaker: Gus Manger
65.text: “I think he is fully focused on Gasom these days. His entire reputation is bound to this corporation now."

66.speaker: Player
66.text: “What's in the past shouldn't shape our future. Especially if a good deal can be talked through.”

67.speaker: Player
67.text: “The feeling is mutual. Both of us are only here because of you, Gus.”

68.speaker: Gus Manger
68.text: “It's one of Sordland's most significant private corporations. Ewald's reputation as chairman and ex-CEO rests on it.”

69.speaker: Gus Manger
69.text: “Yes, and Sordland needs any deal it can get. Soon the term budget will be determined and expenditures won't recover the economy.”

70.speaker: Gus Manger
70.text: “I do my best. Got a close influential contact in Porte Drazon who opened a lot of doors a few years ago.”

71.speaker: Gus Manger
71.text: “Moreover, we have an opportunity to make a larger economic impact on the people of Narbel.”

72.speaker: Gus Manger
72.text: “We can't provide services to our people without corporations like Gasom filling our coffers."

76.speaker: Player
76.text: “I wasn't against him early on. Quite the opposite.”

77.speaker: Gus Manger
77.text: "I still remember the day the party leadership changed from Tarquin Soll. What a historic moment that was.”

79.speaker: Player
79.text: “The fact that you managed to get Rizia entangled in this is surprising.”

80.speaker: Player
80.text: “If he needs to be hands-on as chairman, then the business must not be doing well.”

81.speaker: Player
81.text: "What's so extraordinary about another corporation trying to make a hefty profit off the back of the people?"

85.speaker: Player
85.text: “I have no ill-will against Ewald Alphonso.”

86.speaker: Gus Manger
86.text: “Human greed is undeniable. I always saw it as an asset to move wealth our way, to Sordland.”

87.speaker: Gus Manger
87.text: “It's true that it's seen a lack of consistent growth.”

88.speaker: Gus Manger
88.text: “As you know, he and I go back a long time. He isn't the sell-out some Sollists painted him to be.”

90.speaker: Gus Manger
90.text: “But Gasom is beyond that. Not many nations have such an influential and valuable asset. We ought to maximize its potential.”

91.speaker: Gus Manger
91.text: “But Gasom has the potential to rival global corporations like Rizian Royal Gold. It could be *the* gas exporter."

92.speaker: Player
92.text: "Not exactly the most pleasant location for a meeting, is it?"

93.speaker: Gus Manger
93.text: "I trust Ministers Walda and Beniwoll didn't overwhelm you with their demands."

94.speaker: Player
94.text: “Good to see you, Gus. I wanted to talk to you about what we can do to help the development here.”

95.speaker: Player
95.text: “I would be surprised if there are no demands or expectations here today.”

96.speaker: Player
96.text: "It's a relief to have a break from all that, even if just for a little while."

97.speaker: Gus Manger
97.text: “Petr Vectern isn't the only one you can have fun with, you know! Jokes aside, you are the President, so do what you want!”

102.speaker: Gus Manger
102.text: “No demands from me, President Rayne. I'm all about making deals and finding common ground.”

103.speaker: Gus Manger
103.text: “Perfect. That's exactly what I hope to accomplish during today's discussions. My job is to improve the conditions of places like these.”

104.speaker: Gus Manger
104.text: “Sipping Borin wine at the Jewel beach resort in Benfi would be better, yes.”

105.speaker: Gus Manger
105.text: “Except for running the country to the ground, please.”

106.speaker: Gus Manger
106.text: “If there's one thing Gus Manger stands for, it's win-win solutions.”

107.speaker: Gus Manger
107.text: “The methods for achieving better living standards can be discussed in detail when we talk terms.”

108.speaker: Gus Manger
108.text: "But you know, as someone who has never experienced the working-class way of life, it's important for me to understand why my role holds such significance."

109.speaker: Gus Manger
109.text: “Kris Schar and the company still have many things they need to figure out, but they are good at what they do.”

110.speaker: Gus Manger
110.text: “We won't ignore it, Mr. President. But as I mentioned before, I don't think this new Assembly bill is the way.”

111.speaker: Gus Manger
111.text: “Too few large corporations own too much power. Market economics won't succeed with monopolies.”

112.speaker: Gus Manger
112.text: “If I had any extra time or resources left, I'd enter the construction business myself.”

113.speaker: Gus Manger
113.text: “Anyway, I digress. Let's get to the elevator.”

114.speaker: Player
114.text: “Keep up with the times. Your knowledge will come in handy.”

115.speaker: Player
115.text: “I'm still not sure how fattening your own wallet helps our rural populations."

116.speaker: Player
116.text: “That's going to be me one day.”

117.speaker: Player
117.text: “I don't care about the books. My worry is our duty and service.”

119.speaker: Player
119.text: “I see your point, but the economy is a complex beast.”

120.speaker: Gus Manger
120.text: “We can discuss this later, Mr. Rayne. We shouldn't keep our former president waiting.”

121.speaker: Gus Manger
121.text: “They don't, but it affects them nonetheless.”

122.speaker: Gus Manger
122.text: “Of course it wasn't just Rizia. But their contribution led to interest from other nations like Qinal and Lespia.”

123.speaker: Player
123.text: “I understand. Support the business, and we support the economy.”

124.speaker: Gus Manger
124.text: “I highly advise us to find a middle-ground. If the state can assist Gasom through these tough times, we'll all benefit."

125.speaker: Gus Manger
125.text: “Isn't that paraphrasing Malenyev? Keep in mind we only have a single term to work with.”

126.speaker: Gus Manger
126.text: “Our country needs steadiness and stability more than ever. Yes, we need to fix inequality. But not at the expense of everything else.”

127.speaker: Gus Manger
127.text: “Think of Gasom as a house of cards with an entire city built atop it."

128.speaker: Gus Manger
128.text: “And none of the average citizens here care about anything other than direct support.”

129.speaker: Player
129.text: “Why are there so many workers from abroad?”

130.speaker: Player
130.text: “The whole complex feels very hands-on deck. I can tell an intricate operation when I see one.”

131.speaker: Gus Manger
131.text: “It took decades for Ewald -- and the workers, of course -- to create an enterprise of such global competitive potential.”

132.speaker: Gus Manger
132.text: “The best talent in Sordland was snatched by the SSC in the 1930s. Most other corporations couldn't contend, so they had to look elsewhere."

133.speaker: Gus Manger
133.text: “The equipment provided is high-standard. I've seen it for myself. Besides, there will always be differences between workers.”

134.speaker: Player
134.text: “The white-collars seem to be having it good in here while the majority are working out in the cold.”

135.speaker: Gus Manger
135.text: “Ah, here's the elevator. Ewald ought to be up there already; there's a separate entrance by the helipad."

136.speaker: Player
136.text: “Pat yourself on the back, Gus. You did well. I expect the same and more in my term.”

137.speaker: Gus Manger
137.text: “That's what I liked about Ewald Alphonso. He didn't let titles or rules get in the way of results.”

138.speaker: Gus Manger
138.text: “It was more complicated than that. Obstructionists in the institutions halted critical policies that could have avoided us the recession.”

139.speaker: Gus Manger
139.text: “It's a hundred percent with me. I have some new ideas I'm discussing with Mr. Holl.”

140.speaker: Gus Manger
140.text: “I'm glad we have overcome the worst of those days. The economy isn't great, but it is more stable."

141.speaker: Gus Manger
141.text: “Good leadership is allowing people to excel in what they are good at, not forcing them.”

142.speaker: Gus Manger
142.text: “Yes, the privatization and the cancellation of old policies was too fast and radical, but that wasn't it. The geopolitical pressures on the market were significant.”

147.speaker: Gus Manger
147.text: “Just remember. Past is past. We've got to look to the future."

148.speaker: Gus Manger
148.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_Party_Takeover_Backstab"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_Party_Takeover_Diplomatic"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_Party_CampaignedForAlphonso"] == true) == false)

149.speaker: Narrator
149.text: We stepped into the elevator. Gus punched a code and we began our ascent.

150.speaker: Narrator
150.text: The hallways were lined with doors. Glass panels in them revealed workers in suits and ties, many of foreign origin, busy in their pristine offices.

151.speaker: Player
151.text: “A Qinali architect is an odd choice.”

152.speaker: Gus Manger
152.text: “Some of Gasom's global hires are from the Republic of Qinal. Once you get past the cultural differences, they're really quite gifted.”

156.speaker: Gus Manger
156.text: “Just remember. Alphonso's our friend. We've got the foundation for a great deal.”
156.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_Party_Takeover_Backstab"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_Party_Takeover_Diplomatic"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_Party_CampaignedForAlphonso"] == true)

157.speaker: Gus Manger
157.text: "I have faith that you won't leave us hanging."

158.speaker: Player
158.text: “After your convincing arguments about the railway project, I was curious what else we could achieve."

159.speaker: Gus Manger
159.text: “Sometimes I do it for myself, other times I chase luck with others.”

160.speaker: Player
160.text: “For your sake and mine, I hope you're right."

161.speaker: Player
161.text: “Don't you think it's a little wrong that someone in your position is active in the stock market?”

162.speaker: Player
162.text: “A true capitalist knows how and when to play.”

163.speaker: Gus Manger
163.text: “I like the all-in 3000-share purchase you made. Shows that you're a man of action, like me."

164.speaker: Gus Manger
164.text: "You played it safe with 2000 shares, but you still stand to make some gains.”

165.speaker: Gus Manger
165.text: “Your measly 1000 shares won't make you much profit. But you know, good to dip your feet in the water before taking a dive.”

166.speaker: Gus Manger
166.text: “Me, I got 4000 shares thanks to a low-risk loan I leveraged on an old logistics business of mine.”

167.speaker: Gus Manger
167.text: “The offerings on the Lachaven Stock Exchange aren't bad either. Much better than anything in eastern Merkopa.”

168.speaker: Player
168.text: “How a development minister came to lead such initiatives is beyond me.”

169.speaker: Player
169.text: “Alphonso was the one who nearly brought the depression on us in the first place.”

170.speaker: Player
170.text: “We shouldn't act in a way that jeopardizes Gasom. But we should still do *something*”

171.speaker: Player
171.text: “Sometimes we must destroy our rotten foundations to build something better.”

172.speaker: Player
172.text: “I doubt that a single regional power like Rizia had such an impact.”

173.speaker: Player
173.text: “Look at us, promoting a planned economy while playing our personal wealth for profit in Arcasia.”

174.speaker: Gus Manger
174.text: “You make one wrong move, and the whole thing falls apart."

175.speaker: Gus Manger
175.text: “We made history with the 1950 and 1953 deals. You might remember that the latter agreement prevented a depression just eight months before the elections.”

179.speaker: Gus Manger
179.text: “I hate to brag, but I was the one who opened the gates in Porte Drazon after nearly 32 years of frozen Sordish-Rizia relations.”

180.speaker: Gus Manger
180.text: “Rizia and Sordland were considering a full embargo until Alphonso and I came along."

181.speaker: Gus Manger
181.text: “Ah! I'm flattered, Mr. President. And glad that you made the right choice, of course.”

182.speaker: Player
182.text: “I haven't seen him since the inauguration. He really pulled back from public life.”

183.speaker: Player
183.text: “I'm here because something needs to be done about Narbel's living standards.”

184.speaker: Gus Manger
184.text: “Can you blame the guy? We went full Dwight Walker on him. At least we didn't resort to corporate assassinations.”

185.speaker: Gus Manger
185.text: “Of course. That's going to play a big role in our discussion.”

186.speaker: Gus Manger
186.text: "As soon as the IPO kicks in on the Ventrie City Stock Exchange, we'll both be rolling in Ren."

188.speaker: Player
188.text: “Time for Sordland to think outside of the box and break the game.”

189.speaker: Gus Manger
189.text: “Except the Perla exchange in Lespia, of course."

190.speaker: Gus Manger
190.text: “Not all of the market economy believers are *capitalist pigs*. Look at me, and how many jobs I've brought to this country.”

191.speaker: Gus Manger
191.text: “I don't think so. My job is to bring resources to long-forgotten areas of Sordland and keep our rural areas vitalized.”

192.speaker: Gus Manger
192.text: “What I do during my personal time doesn't affect that. If anything, keeping up with market trends will help me benefit our local economies.”

193.speaker: Gus Manger
193.text: "Anyway, Mr. President, when it comes to money, we either play the game or the game plays us.”

194.speaker: Gus Manger
194.text: “Attract money, invest in the right solutions, increase wealth and living standards. It all trickles down.”

195.speaker: Gus Manger
195.text: “Think of history. Leaders who took big leaps were written in the books.”

196.speaker: Gus Manger
196.text: “Well said! The higher you rise, the less you can fall. Why not pick good people up along the way?”

197.speaker: Gus Manger
197.text: “Well a quarter of my net wealth is on that stock now. But hey, you've got to play big to win big."

199.speaker: Gus Manger
199.text: "Mr. President, I've been brainstorming a little something. The Gruni Rural Investment Plan. I reckon it's got the potential to breathe new life into our rural communities out in Gruni."

200.speaker: Gus Manger
200.text: "We could consider a few things. For starters, we could give the farming business a boost with some subsidies. Or, we could steer towards modernizing existing farms with machinery and tech."

201.speaker: Gus Manger
201.text: "Mr. President, I get the appeal of that GREEN bill that's been making the rounds in the Assembly."

202.speaker: Player
202.text: "I have my doubts, Gus. But I'll give your plan some thought."

203.speaker: Player
203.text: "It's a tough call, Gus. I need to weigh the environmental implications and the economic benefits."

204.speaker: Player
204.text: "Gus, I'm intrigued by your vision. I'll seriously consider your proposal."

205.speaker: Gus Manger
205.text: "I appreciate you hearing me out, Mr. President. I genuinely believe this plan could work wonders for our rural folks."

206.speaker: Gus Manger
206.text: "That's all I'm asking for, Mr. President. Just give this plan a fair shake."

207.speaker: Gus Manger
207.text: "Sure, Mr. President, doubts are part of the game. I trust you'll play the cards right for all of Sordland."

208.speaker: Gus Manger
208.text: "This Workers' Rights Bill... Look, I'm all for giving hard-working folks what they deserve. But, isn't it a bit hasty to push this while we're still stuck in a recession?"

209.speaker: Player
209.text: "In my book, workers' rights aren't up for negotiation, no matter the economic climate."

210.speaker: Player
210.text: "We've got to play this smart. We can't risk another economic blow."

211.speaker: Player
211.text: "Gus, I get what you're saying. But isn't it high time we put people before profits?"

212.speaker: Gus Manger
212.text: "I see where you're coming from, Mr. President. But a prosperous economy helps everyone - the workers included."

213.speaker: Gus Manger
213.text: "Mr. President, I'm glad you're thinking about the big picture. We've got to strike a balance to protect our economy and our workers."

214.speaker: Gus Manger
214.text: "Mr. President, I respect your stance. But let's not forget about the potential fallout."

215.speaker: Gus Manger
215.text: "Or here's another thought - we could pour resources into developing crop breeds tailor-made for Gruni conditions. If it works out, we could roll this out across Sordland."

216.speaker: Gus Manger
216.text: "The way I see it, short-term wins might end up costing us big time in the long run."

217.speaker: Narrator
217.text: Our talk was interrupted by a noise coming from outside the building. We looked out the nearest window.

218.speaker: Gus Manger
218.text: "But I'm telling you, if we put the brakes on that and funnel those funds into the Gruni plan instead, we could make some real strides without spooking any potential investors."

219.speaker: Gus Manger
219.text: "Spectacle aside… before we sit down with him, there's one more Assembly matter I wanted to raise."

220.speaker: Narrator
220.text: On it was our next appointment, Ewald Alphonso.

221.speaker: Player
221.text: "An extravagant show of wealth, isn't it? Hardly seems necessary."

222.speaker: Player
222.text: "That kind of display plays well to investors... but terribly to farmers watching on state TV."

223.speaker: Player
223.text: "Alphonso sure knows how to make an entrance."

225.speaker: Gus Manger
225.text: "Exactly. The optics matter. We just have to decide who we’re trying to impress."

226.speaker: Gus Manger
226.text: "It's Alphonso's style, Mr. President. He's always enjoyed his toys."

227.speaker: Narrator
227.text: A sleek helicopter was cutting through the sky, sunlight glinting off its polished surface as it descended towards us.

228.speaker: Narrator
228.text: He kept talking as he guided me into the Gasom building.

232.speaker: Player
232.text: "I grew up around people like the ones this would help, Gus. If your plan’s solid, I want it to work."

236.speaker: Gus Manger
236.text: "Then we’re on the same page, Mr. President. Let’s make sure they feel seen for once."

237.speaker: Player
237.text: "Is that a helicopter or just his ego with rotor blades?"

238.speaker: Gus Manger
238.text: "He calls it branding. I call it a fuel bill with sound effects."

241.speaker: Gus Manger
241.text: "There's got to be a way to improve workers' rights without rocking the economic boat."

242.speaker: Player
242.text: "Heard a worker from Estord on the radio. Said he's got rights on paper, but nothing in his fridge."

243.speaker: Gus Manger
243.text: "That kind of thing sticks with you. Still, we’ve got to make sure the fixes don’t break something bigger."

244.speaker: Player
244.text: "If we overload businesses now, they'll shrink or shut down. Workers lose more than just rights, they lose jobs."

245.speaker: Player
245.text: "Strong labor protections are the foundation of lasting growth. A secure worker is a productive one."

246.speaker: Player
246.text: "Let’s think of the option that signals progress without rattling the markets. We need both stability and reform."

247.speaker: Player
247.text: "People don’t care about long-term strategy when their kids are hungry now. We fix this for them, or we lose them."

248.speaker: Gus Manger
248.text: "Exactly. We can’t let good intentions gut the economy."

249.speaker: Gus Manger
249.text: "Fair enough, but let’s roll it out in stages. Rushing it could backfire."

250.speaker: Gus Manger
250.text: "That’s the sweet spot. You bring the idealism, I’ll help shape the rollout."

251.speaker: Gus Manger
251.text: "Hard to argue with that. Just make sure we don’t promise more than the treasury can carry."
